description: ForgePass API rate limit tiers. v1 active tiers only. SDK tier reserved as null pending #010 (FR-10-A) resolution.

window.implementation: nestjs-throttler-storage-redis with two-counter blend (current window + previous window weighted by elapsed fraction)
window.rationale: Fixed window ruled out because it allows boundary bursting — a caller can exhaust the full quota at :59 and again at :00, doubling the effective limit. True sliding window log ruled out due to per-request timestamp storage cost at scale (Redis ZADD entry per request). Sliding window counter uses two Redis counters per caller key and blends them by the fraction of the current window elapsed. This prevents boundary bursts in practice, is Redis-native, and requires only a ~30-line extension of the standard @nestjs/throttler guard via nestjs-throttler-storage-redis. No additional library dependency beyond what is already required for distributed rate limit state.

unauthenticated.trust_proxy_note: NestJS app must be configured with app.set('trust proxy', 1) or equivalent so that the real client IP is read from X-Forwarded-For when deployed behind a load balancer. Without this, all unauthenticated requests share the load balancer IP and a single 429 fires after 60 total requests across all users. This configuration belongs in issue #023 (NestJS app core setup).
unauthenticated.scope_rationale: Per-IP-per-endpoint would allow a single IP to consume the full 60/min against /v1/passport/:address and 60/min against /v1/score/:address simultaneously, effectively doubling the real limit for multi-endpoint workflows like a leaderboard render. Per-IP global correctly reflects the intent of the limit.
unauthenticated.rationale: 60 req/min matches the Stellar Horizon public floor (3,600/hr = 60/min), which sets a credible precedent within the Stellar ecosystem and is a number external developers will recognise. It comfortably covers all identified legitimate unauthenticated use cases: developer testing (<10 req/min), active passport explorer browsing (2-8 req/min), and third-party leaderboard page loads (up to 20 req/min burst). At 10,000 contributors and a 60/min limit, scraping the full contributor index from a single IP takes approximately 167 minutes of sustained effort, making casual scraping impractical without IP rotation. IP rotation is a CDN/WAF concern, not a rate limiter concern. Set to 60 rather than 30 (CoinGecko's free floor) because ForgePass's core value proposition is public verifiability — the limit must not 429 a legitimate third-party app on page load, and the leaderboard burst case already reaches 20 req/min.

integrator.rationale: 600 req/min provides 6x headroom above the most demanding identified legitimate integrator workflow: an individual-request leaderboard poller querying 200 contributors every 5 minutes (40 req/min). It covers a Stellar DAO reading governance weights for 50 voters in rapid succession (50 req/min) with substantial room to spare. For batch-based workflows — GrantFox ranking 30 applicants (1-3 req/min), Trustless Work credential feed (<5 req/min) — 600 is not remotely the constraint. Set to 600 rather than 1,000 because: (1) raising a limit is easier than lowering one after integrators are live; (2) at 1,000 req/min a single integrator key could query 1,000 × 100 = 100,000 addresses per minute via the batch endpoint, which is infrastructure headroom not yet validated by load testing (#072); (3) all v1 use cases fit comfortably within 600. The integrator limit should be revisited alongside load test results from #072 and updated in v1.1 if real usage data shows legitimate patterns exceeding the ceiling.

sdk.identification_note: Likely X-ForgePass-SDK-Key or inherited from integrator tier — decision deferred to #010.
sdk.rationale: SDK tier deferred pending #010 (FR-10-A) resolution. The ForgePass SDK is a roadmap item and all FR-10 requirements are deferred in FRD v1.1. The config slot is reserved here so that activating the SDK tier requires only a value change to this file, not a schema change. Any tooling or documentation built against this config structure will not break when #010 resolves. The limit and identification method will be defined at that time.

batch_endpoint.request_weight_rationale: The batch endpoint counts as 1 request against the caller's quota regardless of how many addresses are included (up to the 100-address ceiling). The batch endpoint exists specifically to serve high-volume integrator workflows such as GrantFox applicant ranking. Counting as N addresses would force the integrator limit to exceed 100 purely to accommodate a single full-batch call, which defeats the purpose of the batch endpoint. A motivated abuser can already call 100 individual GET endpoints and retrieve the same data — the batch endpoint is an efficiency feature, not a privilege that warrants additional rate limit penalties. Abuse via the batch endpoint (rapid repeated full-batch calls) is caught by the integrator tier limit regardless of the per-request weight setting.

headers.Retry-After: seconds until the oldest request in the current window expires (sliding window semantics — not a fixed window reset time)
headers.X-RateLimit-Limit: tier limit value for this caller
headers.X-RateLimit-Remaining: requests remaining in the current window at time of response
headers.X-RateLimit-Reset: unix timestamp (seconds) at which the window resets to full capacity

misconfigured_integrator_alerting.threshold: integrator key exceeds limit on 3 consecutive window cycles
misconfigured_integrator_alerting.rationale: A single 429 is expected and handled by retry logic. Sustained rate limit hits across 3 consecutive windows indicate a misconfigured integrator loop, not a burst. An alert (not a block beyond the standard 429) lets the ForgePass team proactively contact the integrator before they raise a support ticket. Consistent with the consecutive-failure alert model established in #004 for the indexer pipeline.

changelog.summary: Initial tier definition. Unauthenticated: 60 req/min per IP (global). Integrator: 600 req/min per X-ForgePass-Key. Batch endpoint: weight 1. Window: sliding window counter, 60s. SDK tier: reserved null pending #010.
changelog.decided_by: ForgePass team internal — no community RFC required
